{{Quote|The lieutenant and I once knew a very fine Human pilot who went by 'Piggy.' There's no 'derogatory component' to it in this squadron. Rather, it's a badge of honor I hope you can live up to.|Wedge Antilles, to Voort saBinring|<ref name="XW:WS">''[[X-Wing: Wraith Squadron]]''</ref>}}
'''Jek Tono Porkins''' was a [[Merchant/Legends|trader]] and [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] from [[Bestine IV/Legends|Bestine IV]] who, along with the other Bestines, was forced to abandon his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] when the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] chose it as the site of a new military base. Seeking the opportunity to strike back at the Empire, Porkins joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] and was assigned to [[Tierfon Rebel Outpost]] for pilot training with the [[Tierfon Yellow Aces/Legends|Tierfon Yellow Aces]]. His skill at low-altitude strafing runs and his rotund physique earned him the nicknames "'''Belly Runner'''" and "'''Piggy'''." After the completion of the Empire's [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]], the Yellow Aces were taken to fully active status and transferred to fill gaps in pilot rosters at other Rebel bases. When Porkins's good friend [[Wes Janson/Legends|Wes Janson]] was taken ill with a case of [[Hesken Fever]], Porkins was given his friend's assignment instead and transferred to [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Red Squadron]], operating out of the [[Great Temple/Legends|Great Temple]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]].

Porkins soon took part in his first missions with Red Squadron, working with [[Biggs Darklighter/Legends|Biggs Darklighter]], [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]], and [[Cesi Eirriss]] to help [[Mission to Commenor (0 BBY)|retrieve]] a number of [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droids]] from the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Nera Dantels]] on [[Commenor/Legends|Commenor]]. The group returned to Yavin 4 just before the arrival of the Death Star in the [[Yavin system/Legends|Yavin system]], on a mission to destroy the Rebel base. Porkins flew as [[Red Six/Legends|Red Six]] during the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], his skills at strafing aiding the Rebels early in the battle. However, when his [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighter]] was struck by debris, leaving him with several mechanical and [[Computer/Legends|computer]] malfunctions, Porkins was hit by enemy [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolaser]] fire and killed.

==Biography==
===Early life===
A native of the [[Bestine system/Legends|Bestine system]], Porkins was a champion [[T-16 skyhopper/Legends|T-16 skyhopper]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] on his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Bestine IV/Legends|Bestine IV]]. During his youth, he spent many years hunting [[sink-crab]]s on the [[Planet/Legends|world's]] rocky islands. He eventually became a [[Merchant/Legends|free trader]] and had just gone into business for himself when the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], seeking to create a new base in that part of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], forced the Bestines from their homeworld and turned the planet into a secure base of operations. When Imperial promises of a new home turned out to be empty, the displaced natives adopted a nomadic lifestyle, wandering aimlessly through their [[Star system/Legends|system]].<ref name="GG1" />

The [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] soon learned of the Bestines' fate and offered them the chance of a new life by joining the fledgling Rebellion against the Empire. Most refused to join the Rebels, unwilling to start a life away from the Bestine system and opting instead to gather the resources they would need to retake their world. Porkins, however, knew that this would take decades and wanted to strike back at the Empire immediately. By joining the Rebel Alliance, he saw his chance to do so and hoped that he could one day persuade the Rebel leadership to help liberate his homeworld.<ref name="GG1" />

===Tierfon Yellow Aces===
{{Quote|Hold your Gandoks, I'm goin' in!|Jek Tono Porkins|<ref name="GG1" />}}
[[File:Porkins3.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Jek Tono Porkins]]
Porkins was initially assigned to [[Tierfon Rebel Outpost]],<ref name="GG3">''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref> serving in the [[Tierfon Yellow Aces/Legends|Tierfon Yellow Aces]].<ref name="XW:WS" /> The Yellow Aces were officially a training [[Squadron/Legends|squadron]] but were frequently involved in the less hazardous active combat missions, giving them combat experience.<ref name="GG3" /> Porkins found the transition from T-16 to [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|BTL Y-wing]] and [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighter]] pilot easy. He soon reached the rank of [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]] and, in under 40 hours of combat time, achieved sixteen confirmed kills.<ref name="GG1" /> Among those in Porkins's training class was a pilot named [[Wes Janson/Legends|Wes Janson]], with whom he worked well and became good friends.<ref name="GG3" /> He and Janson also became acquainted with the young pilot [[N'dru Suhlak]], whom they gave some informal training.<ref name="Slave Ship">''[[Slave Ship]]''</ref> During his time with the Yellow Aces, Porkins acquired his [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]], [[R5-D8/Legends|R5-D8]], who remained with him throughout his career.<ref name="Hasbro">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Power of the Jedi|pack=Jek Porkins (X-Wing Pilot)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/potjporkins.asp}}</ref>

On one mission, the Yellow Aces were sent to ambush an Imperial [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] and its [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighter]] escort as they landed at a temporary Imperial staging base. The squadron flew Y-wings and was under instruction to split into two groups, with one group strafing the base and drawing away its defenses while the other attempted to disable the freighter. The first stage of the mission went well, but when the freighter arrived with a larger escort than expected, Yellow Ace member [[Kissek Doran]] panicked and broke formation. Knowing that if Doran was seen by the Imperials, the Yellow Aces would be compromised and potentially eliminated, Porkins and Janson were ordered to pursue him and attempt to bring him back. If they were unable to do so, they were authorized to shoot him down. Porkins attempted to use his own starfighter to force Doran to the ground. However, his attempts were unsuccessful and Janson was forced to open fire. His [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannon]] cracked Doran's cockpit and he was killed by exposure to the [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]] outside.<ref name="XW:WS" />

In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]],<ref name="NEC" /> with the Alliance becoming aware of the threat posed by the Empire's new [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]], the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]], the Yellow Aces were taken to fully active status. High-security bases were given priority for the newly active pilots and, when [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Red Squadron]] operating out of the Rebel base in the [[Great Temple/Legends|Great Temple]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] needed pilots to fill an immediate shortage, Janson was scheduled for an emergency transfer to the [[Yavin system/Legends|Yavin system]]. However, when Janson was taken ill with [[Hesken Fever]], Porkins took his place.<ref name="GG3" />

===Red Squadron===
{{Quote|That's a good-sized pot.''"<br />"''And he won a lot of credits, too.|Wedge Antilles and Biggs Darklighter, after losing to Porkins at sabacc|<ref name="XWRS0.5">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron ½|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' ½]]</ref>}}
Soon after arriving on Yavin, Porkins attended a briefing by [[General/Legends|General]] [[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Jan Dodonna]]. The Alliance was in need of additional [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] and had recently learned of a number of X-wings at an [[Incom Corporation/Legends|Incom Corporation]] assembly facility. Dodonna outlined a plan to capture the fighters by using four TIE/LN starfighters, recently brought to the Alliance by the defecting crew of the [[Imperial II-class frigate|Class II Frigate]] [[Rand Ecliptic/Legends|''Rand Ecliptic'']], to draw the defending TIE fighters away from the nearby [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]] base. Once the Incom facility was undefended, the ''Rand Ecliptic'' would arrive to retrieve the X-wings. The mission was a success, with the Rebels capturing several of the new starfighters, though [[Peate Kurin]] was killed and [[Derek Klivian/Legends|Derek Klivian]] lost a leg during the diversionary raid. Porkins later joined [[Biggs Darklighter/Legends|Biggs Darklighter]], [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]], and [[Cesi Eirriss]] in practicing in the captured fighters. After visiting Klivian in the infirmary, the group was called back for another briefing with General Dodonna.<ref name="Empire12" />

Though the Alliance now had a supply of starfighters at Yavin 4, they still needed astromech droids to help their pilots operate the [[Starship/Legends|ships]]. The Empire seemed to have anticipated their need and responded with strict controls over the [[Droid/Legends|droids]],<ref name="Empire12" /> but a source had been found when [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Nera Dantels]] of the ''[[Starduster]]'' arranged to take a shipment of [[R2-series astromech droid/Legends|R2]] and [[R5-series astromech droid|R5]] units to the Imperial stronghold of [[Commenor/Legends|Commenor]]. Porkins, along with Darklighter, Antilles, and Eirriss, was [[Mission to Commenor (0 BBY)|dispatched]] undercover to the world to rendezvous with the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]].<ref name="XWRS0.5" />

[[File:Porkins4.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Porkins takes exception to a remark about his size.]]
After arriving at Commenor, the Rebels landed their X-wings at the [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]], rented a [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeder]], and headed to a local [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]],<ref name="XWRS0.5" /> where they had been told to play a game of [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]] while waiting for Dantels.<ref name="Empire12" /> While there, they watched the latest news of the dissolution of the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]] on the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]], learning of the apparent disappearance of [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]]. Porkins won the sabacc game, but as they prepared to play another, Antilles received a signal from Dantels telling them to meet her at [[Hangar Bay 31]], and the group departed. Outside, they were met by a number of local ruffians who claimed to have chased some thieves away from the landspeeder and demanded a reward. When Porkins refused to play along, one of the gang insulted him, causing the Rebel to knee the youth in the midsection. The situation rapidly descended into a brawl, before the Rebels ended the fight by pulling their [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]] and left in the speeder to head to their rendezvous.<ref name="XWRS0.5" />

The Rebels finally met with Captain Dantels and examined the cargo of astromechs. After confirming the cargo, they arranged to meet up with her in orbit and lead the ''Starduster'' back to Yavin 4. However, unknown to the Rebels, one of the street gang had followed them, leading a [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] to the meeting. The stormtrooper called the [[Folor Base|Imperial base]] on the nearby [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Folor]] to warn them of the fleeing Rebels. By the time the Rebels collected their X-wings and reached orbit, the Imperials had already dispatched TIE/LN starfighters to intercept them.<ref name="XWRS0.5" />

Seeing the incoming fighters, Antilles and Darklighter broke formation to intercept, leaving Porkins and Eirriss to provide cover for the ''Starduster''. Nevertheless, some TIEs made it through and were able to get on Porkins's tail. Eirriss eliminated his pursuers and Porkins soon reciprocated, but more TIEs came and attacked the ''Starduster''. Though Dantels was able to shoot them off, some of the debris struck Eirriss's X-wing, damaging her [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|shield generator]] and [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]]. With no time to eject before the next wave of TIEs arrived, and no way to leave the system, Eirriss set a collision course for the incoming fighters, telling her comrades to leave without her. Her X-wing was destroyed in a head-on collision with the Imperial fighters.<ref name="XWRS0.5" />

Porkins, Antilles, and Darklighter jumped to [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]], leading the ''Starduster'' back to Yavin 4. After landing in the Great Temple, and learning that the Death Star was already en route to Yavin to destroy the Rebel base, the Rebel pilots agreed to dedicate the destruction of the [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] to their fallen comrade.<ref name="XWRS0.5" /> On Porkins's recommendation, Yellow Ace pilot [[John D. Branon/Legends|John D. Branon]] was selected to take the place of Eirriss for the upcoming [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|battle]].<ref name="TEGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> Soon after returning, Porkins met Darklighter's old friend, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], who had himself just arrived on Yavin 4 and was also to join Red Squadron.<ref name="XWRS0.5" />

===Battle of Yavin===
{{Quote|I've got a problem here.''"<br />"''Eject.''"<br />"''I can hold it.''"<br />"''Pull up!''"<br />"''No, I'm all&mdash;Aargh!|Porkins talks to Darklighter, moments before his death|audio=DeepFriedPorkins.flac|<ref name="ANH" />}}
[[File:Jek_Porkins_X-Wing_XWM.png|thumb|left|260px|Jek Porkins during the Battle of Yavin]]
Soon, the Death Star arrived in the system, but the Rebels believed they had found a weakness in the battlestation. [[Death Star plans/Legends|Plans]] provided by Leia Organa after her rescue from Imperial capture had revealed a small [[Thermal exhaust port/Legends|thermal exhaust port]] leading to the main [[Reactor/Legends|reactor core]]. With the Death Star's defenses geared towards defending the station from a large-scale attack, the Rebels believed it would be possible for their starfighters to navigate down a narrow trench on the Death Star's surface, and fire a [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedo]] into the exhaust port, triggering a chain reaction that would destroy the station. After General Dodonna outlined the mission, the Rebel pilots prepared for battle.<ref name="ANH" /> As the Rebels rushed to get ready for the battle, the [[Red 6|X-wing]] assigned to Porkins missed its final inspection of [[Computer/Legends|computer]] and flight control systems.<ref name="red6">{{CCG|set=A New Hope Limited|cardname=Red 6}}</ref> 

[[File:Roasted_Porkins.png|thumb|285x285px|Porkins dies as his X-wing disintegrates around him.]]
Porkins flew under the [[Callsign/Legends|call sign]] [[Red Six/Legends|Red Six]] during the Battle of Yavin. After arriving at the approaching battlestation, the Rebels initiated strafing runs in the area around the trench.<ref name="ANH" /> Porkins's skill with strafing played an important part in the success of the early runs,<ref name="red6" /> but the Rebel fighters came under heavy fire from a [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolaser]] emplacement near one of the surface's many [[deflection tower]]s. Darklighter moved to attack the tower, telling Porkins to provide cover. The two pilots dived towards the surface, opening fire on the tower and scoring a direct hit.<ref name="ANH" /> However, as the tower exploded, Porkins was caught by debris from the blast, causing instruments throughout his fighter to malfunction.<ref name="ivegotaproblemhere">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=I've Got A Problem Here}}</ref> Though his X-wing fighter was generally maneuverable enough to avoid the Death Star's sluggish turbolasers, incorrect readings from his instrumentation left him unable to judge his altitude and he found himself too low and an easy target for enemy fire.<ref name="ANH novel">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novelization]]</ref> Darklighter attempted to warn his friend that he was too low and advised him to eject, but Porkins felt that he could control the problem. Before he was able to regain control, however, he was hit by enemy turbolaser fire and was killed as his X-wing exploded around him.<ref name="ANH" />

===Legacy===
{{Quote|You are elite pilots and you are more than just that, but no matter who you are, or how good you are, you'll never be considered as good as Biggs Darklighter or Jek Porkins or anyone else who has died in service to Rogue Squadron. They are legends, this unit is a legend, and none of us are ever going to be able to be more than they are.|Wedge Antilles addresses members of Rogue Squadron|<ref name="XW:RS">''[[X-Wing: Rogue Squadron]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Porkins2.jpg|thumb|left|265x265px|Holographic memorial to Porkins on Yavin 4]]
A [[Hologram/Legends|holographic]] memorial to Porkins, along with the other pilots killed during the mission, was installed in the Great Temple following the battle.<ref name="Empire15">[[Empire 15|''Empire'' 15]]</ref> His actions during the Battle of Yavin saw him posthumously awarded the [[Kenobi Medallion]], a medal created specifically to remember the sacrifices of those who fought at Yavin. His Kenobi Medallion was hung with those of his comrades in the pilots' lounge at Tierfon Rebel Base.<ref name="GG1" /> Red Squadron survivors Luke Skywalker and Wedge Antilles later founded [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]]<ref name="GG3" /> and around ten [[Standard month/Legends|months]] after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]<ref name="Rogue Squadron Omnibus 3">''[[Star Wars Omnibus: X-Wing Rogue Squadron Volume 3]]''</ref> of [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="NEC" /> though Porkins died before Rogue Squadron's formation, Antilles reflected about having always considered him and the other members of Red Squadron to be among the first Rogues during a [[Funeral of Rebel and New Republic pilots|funeral]] held to honor members who were killed in the [[Battle of Brentaal IV (Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Brentaal IV]].<ref name="RS26">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 26|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 26]]</ref> Rogue Squadron named one of their maneuvers [[Porkins' Formation]] in his memory.<ref name="TLC">''[[The Last Command]]''</ref>

Porkins was still included in the Rogue Squadron memorial as late as [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]].<ref name="MR4">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 35|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 35]]</ref><ref name="5ABY">''[[Star Wars Omnibus: X-Wing Rogue Squadron Volume 3]]'' places the events of ''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron: Mandatory Retirement]]'' approximately one year after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], which ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' places in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].</ref> After Antilles and Janson formed [[Wraith Squadron]], they informed the [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]] Wraith recruit [[Voort saBinring]] that they did not see his nickname of "Piggy" as an insult; instead it was a legacy to live up to as the same nickname had once belonged to Porkins.<ref name="XW:WS" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|The Empire or Us&mdash;there is no compromise. Biggs Darklighter, Wedge Antilles, Jek Porkins.|Engraved by the Rebel pilots on the Great Temple prior to the Battle of Yavin|<ref name="I, Jedi">''[[I, Jedi]]''</ref>}}
A [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]]<ref name="GG1" /> with [[Color/Legends|blue]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and brown [[Hair/Legends|hair]] which was turning gray by his time with Red Squadron,<ref name="Empire12" /> Porkins was 1.8 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall<ref name="height" /> and weighed 110 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]].<ref name="H2H" /> His large physical stature, together with his skills at strafing, earned him the nickname "Belly Runner".<ref name="GG1" /> His build also earned him the nickname "Piggy".<ref name="XW:WS" /> Porkins never objected to his friends joking about his size, which he attributed to the high [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]] on Bestine IV, though on at least one occasion he reacted angrily to comments from an outsider.<ref name="XWRS0.5" />

As a heavyset man, Porkins would set his [[Acceleration compensator/Legends|inertial compensator]] to full while in flight. Wedge Antilles always considered this a possible factor in his death&mdash;had his compensation been lower, he may have realized how low he was and been able to attempt to correct it before he was struck by enemy fire.<ref name="XW:RS" />

Despite his unflattering nicknames, Porkins made many friends among those he served with and was seen as both brave and noble and was one of the most respected pilots in the Rebel Alliance.<ref name="GG1" /> His good friend Wes Janson often spoke highly of him, though Janson struggled with the guilt he felt about his absence from Yavin, feeling that this had contributed to Porkins's death.<ref name="GG3" /> 

==Skills and abilities==
Porkins was capable in unarmed combat<ref name="Empire12" /> and a capable pilot whose experience hunting sink-crabs helped him become a specialist in strafing runs during his time as a Rebel pilot. He was also a competent [[Starfighter combat/Legends|dogfighter]], amassing an impressive number of kills in his career.<ref name="GG1" /> Wedge Antilles also considered Porkins to be among the best pilots he had flown with and was deeply hurt by his death.<ref name="XW:RS" />

==Equipment==
Porkins wore the standard [[Rebel flight suit]] along with a [[Flight helmet/Legends|flight helmet]] and [[Goggles/Legends|goggles]]<ref name="ANH" /> and he wielded a [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]].<ref name="Movie Heroes">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Movie Heroes|pack=Yavin Pilot Pack|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/Yavin-Pilot-Pack-2012-Movie-Heroes-Multipack.asp}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
===Possibly porcine===
Jek Porkins was created by [[George Lucas]] for the [[original trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], in which he was played by [[William Hootkins]].<ref name="ANH" /> The film released on [[May 25]], [[1977]].<ref name="Year">''[[Star Wars Year by Year: A Visual Chronicle]]''</ref> Hootkins was originally considered to stand in for the then-[[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]]. However, after reading the script, Hootkins was unsure about the film and decided to take a different job. When his other work finished, Hootkins learned that Lucas was still seeking actors to play Rebel pilots and decided to take one of the parts.<ref name="Insider32" />

[[File:PorkinsPromo.jpg|thumb|right|300px|William Hootkins during the filming of ''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope''.]]
With so many roles involving heavy make-up, Hootkins initially wondered if the name Porkins might imply he was to have pig-like make-up applied and had to check with Lucas to confirm his character's species was Human. The Rebel pilot uniforms had been made to a standard size and Hootkins's costume had to be slit down the back in order to fit him, slightly exposing his [[Wikipedia:Mr. Natural (comics)|Mr. Natural]] T-shirt underneath. Cramped into the small [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]] for his character's explosive death scene, Hootkins initially thought the actors playing Death Star crewmembers had the better roles but would later consider himself lucky to have played one of the film's heroic Rebels.<ref name="Insider32">{{InsiderCite|32|Rebel Pilot Reunion}}</ref>

===Adaptation differences===
{{Quote|So long, Piggy. You will be avenged!|Biggs Darklighter's thoughts on the death of Porkins|<ref name="SW6">[[Star Wars (1977) 6|''Star Wars'' (1977) 6]]</ref>}}
The Porkins character first appeared in [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]] of the film<ref name="ANH novel" /> ghostwritten by [[Alan Dean Foster]]<ref name="ANH novel SE">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novelization]], [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|''Special Edition'']] foreword by [[George Lucas]]</ref> and published in [[1976]]. In the book his call sign was given as [[Blue Four/Legends|Blue Four]],<ref name="ANH novel" /> which the original script of ''A New Hope'' also used, before being later changed to [[Red Four/Legends|Red Four]]. Porkins remained as Red Four until shooting when he changed once more to the final Red Six, with Branon becoming Red Four. This is the likely explanation for another pilot calling for Red Six after Porkins has been killed.<ref name="DB" />

In the [[Star Wars (1977) 6|sixth issue]] of the [[Marvel Comics|Marvel]] [[Star Wars (1977)|comic adaptation]] of the film, written by [[Roy Thomas]] and [[Howard Chaykin]]<ref name="SW6" /> and published on [[September 13|September 13,]] 1977,<ref name="Marvel6Date">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/53796/star_wars_1977_6|text=Star Wars (1977) #6}} {{C|On-sale date is noted in backup link.}}</ref> Porkins was given the call sign [[Blue Six/Legends|Blue Six]] and was depicted as being killed by a TIE fighter after his mechanical malfunction.<ref name="SW6" /> The nickname "Piggy" was first used in Foster's novel<ref name="ANH novel" /> and also appeared in ''Star Wars 6'', in a panel in which Darklighter briefly mourns the death of his friend. ''Star Wars 6'' was also the first source to provide the character with a first name, calling him Tono Porkins.<ref name="SW6" />

''[[The Star Wars Storybook]]'', authored by [[Geraldine Richelson]] and published in [[1978]], swaps the roles of Red and [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Gold Squadrons]]. The pilot identified as [[Gold Six/Legends|Gold Six]] is killed by a TIE fighter around the same time as Skywalker saves Darklighter from another TIE.<ref name="TWSS">''[[The Star Wars Storybook]]''</ref> In the movie, this event occurs after Porkins has been killed, and it is Branon who is killed during the initial TIE attack.<ref name="ANH" />

In the [[1981]]<ref name="Highlights">{{WebCite|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-courier-journal-radio-highlights/77115604/|text=Radio Highlights|work=The Courier-Journal|date=1981-05-25|archivedate=20240124044310}}</ref> [[Star Wars (radio)|''Star Wars'' radio]] episode "[[Force and Counterforce]]," Porkins is involved in a dogfight against TIE fighters during the Battle of Yavin. After the Imperial fighters are launched in response to the Rebel assault, Porkins attacks one of the TIEs which is pursuing Red Four. He subsequently assists [[Garven Dreis/Legends|Red Leader]] in locating Skywalker when his X-wing passes through a heavy fire zone.<ref name="TNPRD">[[Star Wars: The National Public Radio Dramatization|''Star Wars'': The National Public Radio Dramatization]]</ref> This contradicts the events of the movie, in which Porkins is killed before the TIE fighter attack, and [[Theron Nett/Legends|Red Ten]] takes his place in the exchange with [[Red Leader/Legends|Red Leader]].<ref name="ANH" /> In the same episode, Porkins' death is not depicted directly, but it is implied later when he fails to report in with the other Red pilots.<ref name="TNPRD" />

===Naming and prop reuse===
[[File:KasanMoor.png|thumb|left|250px|The Kasan Moor character reused Jek Porkins's helmet.]]
[[Grant S. Boucher]]'s [[1989]] [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] sourcebook ''[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope]]'' later gave the character the first name "Jek,"<ref name="GG1" /> despite reciving the first name "Tono" in the comic adaptaton.<ref name="SW6" />
The contradiction with the character's name remained publicly unresolved until [[March 12]], [[2002]].<ref name="SW.com">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/other/rpg/news20020222.html|text=Starfighters Soar in Gamer #9}} indicates that [[Star Wars Gamer 9|''Star Wars Gamer'' 9]] shipped to subscribers on [[February 22]], [[2002]], and both issues 8 and 10 were sent to newstands 18 days after their subscriber ship date; thus, ''Star Wars Gamer'' 9 was published on [[March 12]].</ref> When [[Josh Radke]] wrote the article "[[Wraith Squadron: The Dirty Dozen of Star Wars|Wraith Squadron: The Dirty Dozen of ''Star Wars'']]" for [[Star Wars Gamer 9|''Star Wars Gamer'' 9]], he asked [[Abel G. Peña]] to see if there was anything else to add to the article. Peña suggested that they take the opportunity to resolve the two names. Previous name contradictions had been resolved by [[Retroactive continuity|retconning]] one as a nickname, but with "Piggy" and "Belly Runner" already used as such, this was quickly ruled out. Instead, Peña suggested using Tono as the character's middle name. Radke agreed with the idea and the article reflected his full name as Jek Tono Porkins.<ref name="Blog-abelgpena|26">{{Blog|abelgpena|26|R.I.P. Jek Tono Porkins}}</ref>

Porkins's helmet prop was later reused by the [[1987]] [[Star Tours (real-world)|Star Tours]] attraction's [[Red Leader (Star Tours)|Red Leader]] character,<ref name="Star Tours">[[Star Tours (real-world)|''Star Tours'']]</ref> and by the pilot [[Kasan Moor/Legends|Kasan Moor]] in the [[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']] video game from [[1998]].<ref name="SWRS">[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']]</ref> Both match the photo of the worn helmet prop in the ''[[Star Wars Costumes: The Original Trilogy]]'' book.<ref name="Costumes">''[[Star Wars Costumes: The Original Trilogy]]''</ref>
